evidence: Route 5 (block structure) + route 1 applied to a published correlation matrix; re-runnable as verify_lee_2024_panas.R. (a) Under the shipped K-PANAS order (PA = positions 1,4,5,8,9,12,14,17,18,19) the live 20x20 matrix gives mean within-valence r = 0.400 and between-valence r = -0.007, gap 0.407, with all 20/20 items closer to their own block; under the canonical Watson et al. (1988) order the same statistics are 0.200 / 0.170 / 0.030. (b) Park et al. (2022) Sustainability 14:16456 Table 1 publishes the full 20x20 K-PANAS correlation matrix for an independent Korean college sample (N=875), with adjectives named per item in its Table 3. The two 190-entry lower triangles correlate r = 0.968; published r(C13,C20) = 0.71 vs live r(PANAS13,PANAS20) = 0.72 and r(C16,C20) = 0.65 vs live 0.67; the globally optimal one-to-one (Hungarian) assignment of the 20 live profiles to the 20 published profiles is the identity, 20/20 fixed points, matched-profile sum 19.11 against 0.90 (SD 3.86) over 20000 random relabellings, p < 5e-5. Per-item argmax is the identity for 16/20; the 4 near-ties are within-facet neighbours. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: PANAS13 (scared) and PANAS20 (afraid) are not separated -- swapping only those two labels changes Frobenius ||P-C||^2 from 1.895 to 1.865, i.e. no worse, so their assignment rests on Park et al. (2022) Table 3 alone. Hence PARTIAL rather than VERIFIED.

route: explicit numeric item labels (source column names) + route 1 (published per-item Rasch difficulty vs live number correct)
evidence: data/lee_2025_nursing_exam.py maps raw .tab columns '1'..'50' to item_01..item_50 by a number-preserving rename, and Supplement 1 prints the exam's items under those same numbers 1-50, so code and text are tied by a label match across all 50 items. Corroborated against the deposit's Supplement 5, which publishes a Rasch difficulty per item.id 1-50 fitted to these same 117 examinees: reading the live table in order item_01..item_50, Spearman(published b, number correct) = -1.0000 exactly (b rounded to 5dp; the raw estimates for equally-scored items differ in the 8th decimal), and the tie structure is a bijection -- 30 distinct b values against 30 distinct raw scores, every b-tie group a raw-score tie group and conversely (e.g. b=-0.81027 for items 1, 10 and 32, all with 100/117 correct; b=-3.874591 for item 8 with 116/117; b=+1.963874 for items 3 and 18 with 65 and 66). Twenty items share a raw score with another item, so this statistic ranks the 50 into 30 groups and the label match is what separates items inside a group; a third, independent number-keyed file, Dataset 2 (domains of items), matches the transcribed content item by item (33 = semen analysis/infertility, 40 = fertility rate, 44 = syphilis, 50 = cervical cryotherapy). Re-runnable as verify_lee_2025_nursing_exam.R (VERDICT: PASS).

route: 3 (published subscale key reproduced against the deposit's own subscale aggregates, computed from the live items)
evidence: The official Spanish BREQ-3 form prints a fixed item-number -> subscale key (intrinsic 4,12,18,22; integrated 5,10,15,20; identified 3,9,17; introjected 2,8,16,21; external 1,7,13,19; amotivation 6,11,14,23 -- 23 numbers, each used once). The study's PLOS S1 .sav carries six precomputed subscale MEAN columns. Taking the LIVE IRW items named by that key and row-averaging them reproduces every one of those deposit aggregates for all 1850 respondents with max|diff| = 0.00e+00 (tolerance 1e-9) on all six subscales: Intrinsic 4.6251/4.6251, Integrated 4.5662/4.5662, Identified 4.7027/4.7027, Introjected 2.4846/2.4846, External 1.2923/1.2923, Amotivation 1.3662/1.3662 (deposit/live). Any item assigned across a subscale boundary would break this exactly. Coding direction: intrinsic mean 4.63 vs amotivation 1.37, ascending as shipped, agreeing with the .sav value labels. What this does NOT establish: the order WITHIN a subscale -- BREQ4/BREQ12/BREQ18/BREQ22 are interchangeable under this test, and their individual wording rests on the printed form's own numbering (which is also the deposit's column numbering), not on any statistic. Hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED.
